sections.h2: Where a Vinton County deed gets recorded
sections.html:
Deeds are recorded at the courthouse in McArthur, 100 East Main Street, OH 45651. The recorder answers at 740-596-4314 from 8:30 am to 4:00 pm on weekdays.

Besides deeds and mortgages, the counter takes oil and gas leases, military discharge papers, and tax, unemployment and workers compensation liens. Staff help where they can, but they do not run searches, help with wording or sell blank forms. If you need a deed written, line up a title company or lawyer before the trip.

sections.h2: Selling a house in Vinton County
sections.html:
Vinton County is rural, with about 13,000 people, and McArthur is the seat. Over eighty percent of the land is wooded, and state parks, forests and part of the Wayne National Forest draw hikers, boaters and hunters. Many sales here involve acreage, so expect buyers to ask about tract boundaries, wells and septic systems.

If you are fixing up a house before a sale, the Development Department at 740-596-3529 can tell income-eligible residents about loans or grants for emergency repairs, septic systems or potable water. Rural splits are common, which is why the engineer's office sits at the start of the paperwork trail described below.

The office holds deed books and indexes from 1850 through December 31, 1985. From January 1, 1986 on, the index is searchable on the county's Ava site, with names and index data but no images.

New filings can go in electronically. The office is fully online for transfer documents, and ePN (888-325-3365) and CSC (866-652-0111) are the e-recording routes. Property owners can also enroll in a free fraud alert at propertyfraudalert.com or 1-800-728-3858, which pings them when something is filed against their parcel.

Ohio's section 317.32 prices the opening two pages of an instrument at $34, split into two $17 halves, and each extra page at $8, split $4 and $4. Counties may layer on a preservation charge, capped by the statute at $5. A revised fee schedule and guidelines took effect January 1, 2025, so confirm the total with the office before sending a check.

  • Zoning resolutions: $25 plus $25.
  • Zoning amendments: $10 plus $10.
  • A certified copy: $1 plus $1 per page, and the seal costs 50 cents plus 50 cents.

Every office a seller needs sits at the same address, so one morning can cover the whole list.

Vinton County courthouse offices in a home sale
OfficeRole in a salePhone
EngineerApproves deed and land contract descriptions, keeps tax maps740-790-7014
AuditorStatement of value, conveyance fee, transfers on the tax list740-790-7007
RecorderRecords the deed or mortgage740-596-4314
TreasurerCollects property tax, confirms what is owed740-790-7045
Clerk of CourtsCourt filings, titles and passports740-596-3001

The county engineer approves every deed and land contract description. Splitting a rural tract is common here, so that stop comes first. The auditor's endorsement comes next, and the recorder will not accept the deed without it.

The auditor posts a single conveyance rate of $4.00 per $1,000 of the sale price, for houses and manufactured homes alike. The grantor pays it when the deed is handed to the auditor. State law, in 319.54 and 322.02, allows a $1 per $1,000 fee plus an optional county tax of up to thirty cents per hundred dollars.

The same office keeps the valuation side of the file. State law expects values to land between 90 and 110 percent of market, measured against sales from the preceding three years, and owners were warned to expect a notable jump after the last triennial update. If you think a value is too high, bring a complaint to the Board of Revision, where the auditor serves as secretary beside the treasurer and the president of the commissioners. Complaints must reach the auditor on or before March 31 each year.

The homestead credit shields up to $26,200 of market value from local taxes for qualifying seniors and permanently disabled owners. New applicants need adjusted income under $40,000, so call the auditor for the current limit.

The statute carves out many cases, and a filing in one of them lists the reason instead of a price. These are the likeliest in a family sale:

  • A gift between spouses or from a parent to a child.
  • A deed that fixes an error in an earlier recorded deed.
  • A trust deed the maker can revoke.
  • Property split among heirs for no payment.
  • A transfer to a nonprofit charity without payment.
  • An easement valued at $1,000 or less.

Second-half real estate and manufactured home tax comes due near the end of July. An unpaid second half draws a 5 percent penalty past the due date and 10 percent ten days after, under ORC 323.121. Payment can be made by check, money order, cash or credit card, with 2.75 percent added on cards. A labeled drop box stands in the alley behind the courthouse and the former sheriff's office, and cash does not belong in it.

The county is divided into 18 taxing districts, and rates for residential and agricultural property run per thousand dollars of valuation. For tax year 2025, Brown-Vinton is 34.280207, the Hamden corporation is 43.440994, Zaleski is 43.551322 and the McArthur corporation is 48.162418. Village parcels carry a higher total than township parcels.

If a bill has not arrived, call the treasurer at 740-790-7045, because a title company needs the true balance before closing.

Here is the usual path for a seller.

  • Have a title company or lawyer draft the deed.
  • Take the legal description to the engineer for approval, especially if you are splitting a tract.
  • Bring the approved deed to the auditor, file the statement of value and pay the conveyance fee.
  • Send the endorsed deed to the recorder, in person or through an e-recording route, with the recording fee.

A cash buyer skips the lender's appraisal and underwriting, but these four stops stay the same. Ask the treasurer for the true tax balance first so nothing surprises you at the table.

Bring a photo ID, the signed deed and a check for the fees. If the property is a manufactured home, the same conveyance rate applies, so the auditor treats it like a house. Call ahead if your deed involves heirs, a trust or an easement, since those can change which fees apply. Allow extra time for a rural tract, where the engineer may need to look at the description before anyone else signs off.

faqs.q: What is the phone number for the Vinton County recorder?
faqs.a: The number is 740-596-4314. Weekday counter hours are 8:30 am to 4:00 pm, in the courthouse at 100 East Main Street, McArthur.

faqs.q: Can a deed be e-recorded in Vinton County?
faqs.a: Yes. The recorder accepts transfer documents electronically through ePN and CSC. Paper still goes to the courthouse counter.

faqs.q: How much is the Vinton County conveyance fee?
faqs.a: It is $4.00 per thousand dollars of the sale price, for house and manufactured home sales alike. The seller pays at the auditor's office ahead of recording.

faqs.q: Will the Vinton County recorder help draft a deed?
faqs.a: No. Staff do not search records, help prepare a document or provide recording forms. A title company or attorney should handle the drafting.

faqs.q: How do I get an alert if a document is filed on my Vinton County property?
faqs.a: Enroll in the free fraud alert, either online at propertyfraudalert.com or by phone at 1-800-728-3858. It comes with the recorder's current recording provider.
